question: Which exact-target firmware functions implement the miwear/interconnect named-connection framework that quickapp system.interconnect uses to talk to the phone?
prototype_hypothesis: interconnect_connect(loop, conn, name, cb) registers a named connection on miwear-server; interconnect_send(handle, name, msg, done, arg) queues one message; interconnect_close(conn) tears down a connection; interconnect_loop reads the global 0x20121F90 registry; quickapp_register_app(app_id, app_info) registers a package in the quickapp routing registry.
callsite_evidence: sub_C2D2034 copies name into a 64-byte slot, stores cb at conn+4 and the node at conn[0], and registers on the miwear-server via sub_C2CB828

sub_C2D20C4 walks the connection list matching name (sub_C587530) then queues through sub_C2D1B58; conn+8==0 routes through sub_C2D1D7C which copies the 5-word message header (+0..+16) into the send request
sub_C2D1A0C invokes the send-done callback as (conn, status, msg, arg) with R0=conn R1=status R2=msg R3=arg
sub_C2D2198 queues connection teardown via loc_C2C56B4
sub_C527E38 registers a package in the quickapp routing registry, echoing 'registered quickapp' and handing out sequential app ids via word_200D194E
quickapp_send_wearmsg (sub_C5289A8) resolves the package through sub_C528F5C -> sub_C8CE848 before sending, so a custom package must be registered first
sub_C66B8C0 reads the 'interconnect.appname' config property (default com.xiaomi.miwear.interconnect); the phone routes by package name only
control_flow_evidence: sub_C2D2034 -> sub_C2CB828(owner, node, "miwear-server", handler, arg) confirms the framework is a named-server socket/msq transport
sub_C2D20C4 dispatch: conn[8]==0 -> sub_C2D1D7C (direct connection send), conn[8]!=0 -> named/broadcast walk
sub_CAA35A0 (uv_miwear_message_recv_cb) routes inbound messages to client queues (apps/algo/capture/miconnect) that reconnect into sub_C2D20C4
sub_C8876A0 (jse_miwear.cpp __miwear_connect_cb) maps event status words 2/3/5/6/7 to failure/close/connected/disconnected/uninstalled, matching the CONN_STATUS_* codes
the framework is shared by quickapp jse_miwear.cpp and feature modules/interconnect_impl.cpp; a native module can register the same way without the JS engine
ownership_analysis: conn is a caller-owned buffer of at least 12 bytes for the link lifetime. Messages passed to send must remain valid until the send-done callback fires. Callbacks run on the connection-framework owner thread and must re-enter a module core only through a non-blocking lock.
unsafe_assumptions: STATIC_RECOVERED: signatures recovered from IDA; device probe pending
the phone-side routing for a custom package name depends on the phone app recognizing it
loop handle 0x20121F90 is the quickapp proxy loop; the exact threading context of recv callbacks needs a device probe
recommended_probe: On device, register a test package, open a named connection, send a message, and observe the recv callback under the miwear link; verify the phone delivers by package name.
